report.summary: The proposed source-label fact renderer is directionally sound: it reuses the existing finite html_labels descriptor and the page/form grouping, keeps strict IDs and citations, and does not filter words. However, the negative raw changes_suggested path cannot rest on 'no matching complete page/form group' as the source defines that group today. The current parser silently skips nested xhtml iframe, xmp, noembed, noframes and plaintext content through INERT (assessment-label-citations.ts:15,29). The current 'incomplete' result is chosen from the single largest partial group (lines 107-111), so a complete group behind an XHTML-island boundary is reported as an incomplete group of a different group. The whole-source absence gate ('zero omitted/truncated HTML', item 319 of the fixture) cannot be established from the labels parser or from the supplied packet. The renderer proposal must therefore be specified so that an island, an ownership ambiguity, or an HTML coverage gap yields unknown (manual source clarification) and never a negative absence fact. This reviewer found two concrete counterexamples. First, a form descriptor with one label inside an xmp island. Second, a page descriptor that has a split group and a complete group in a suppressed island.

findings.title: Labels inside foreign HTML islands are silently skipped, so whole-group absence would be a false negative
findings.evidence: Line 29 skips any element whose namespace is not XHTML or whose tag is in INERT. One branch of INERT is excluded: textarea. These elements are not visited and not counted. The INERT set includes iframe, xmp, noembed, noframes and plaintext. For these the parser builds element content rather than text, although HTML5 treats them as raw/escapable text. As a result, markup nested inside them is parsed as element nodes and silently dropped. The label walk at line 51 repeats the same skip. The proposal (fixture line 319) forbids a negative whole-source absence fact unless 'all bounded DOM parses complete', and this condition is not checked. Concretely, xmp is not a rawtext element in HTML5. `<xmp><form><label for=m>E-mail:</label><input id=m></form></xmp>` yields an XHTML form/label tree in parse5. labelsIn drops this subtree as INERT, so a form descriptor sees form 0 missing 'E-mail:' and the proposed renderer could state a whole-source incomplete group.
findings.reproduction: Unexecuted reasoning trace over the supplied parser. Parse `<form><label for=n>Name:</label><input id=n></form><xmp><form><label for=m>E-mail:</label><input id=m></form></xmp>` with scriptingEnabled. labelsIn returns only the Name: label, with form key A. The lines 107-111 incomplete result is form A missing E-mail:. Yet the source does contain an HTML form that holds E-mail:, so the negative fact describes the wrong group. This is the same class of boundary that the proposal itself calls out for foreign islands.
findings.suggestion: Make suppressed-container content a hard unknown. Have the walker record whether any XHTML element inside iframe, xmp, noembed, noframes or plaintext carries label-relevant children. Also record any parse5 'non-void-html-element-start-tag-with-trailing-solidus' error that follows a <label/>. Then have the renderer return unknown unless the HTML scope is fully, exactly parsed and every group owner resolves. Otherwise, explicitly enumerate these island subtrees while walking, instead of silently skipping them.

findings.title: 'No matching complete group' can be claimed from the single largest partial group while another group is complete
findings.evidence: At lines 107-109, lines 96-103 skip any label whose own parts are not fully cited. Only then does line 107 check whether a group is complete. If there are no completely cited groups, line 110 sorts the partial groups and returns 'incomplete' with the labels missing from the best group. A different group that contains all labels is never identified. The known regression data in the fixture shows this in practice. In the MDN case (test/fixture lines 17 and 60-68), contact.html form F holds Name:/Message: and index.html form G holds E-mail:. Group F comes first in the files-sort order at line 89. The model cites s4, s9, s7 and s140 as separate citations, and only G is complete. The fixture result stays 'incomplete'. The proposed renderer keeps 'incomplete' as the accepted negative evidence, and would turn this into a page/form-level absence fact tied to the first/largest group.
findings.reproduction: Unexecuted reasoning trace over the supplied fixture. Criterion 1 is the quoted label list with no context word. Pass these files and citations to the current check. It returns {kind:"incomplete", context:"page", missingLabels:["E-mail:"]} on the strength of contact.html only. If the new renderer says "no page group contains all three labels" from this coverage value, that statement is contradicted by index.html, which does contain an 'E-mail:' label (not the required full set, but the per-file/per-group attribution is lossy). A form-context variant is worse: index.html's trailing form is a real bounded owner, and the chosen group would be whichever file sorts first.
findings.suggestion: Do not derive the negative sentence from the current 'incomplete' value. Return a structured group inventory instead: for each page or form owner, the complete label set and a fully-cited flag. Then emit the negative fact only when every uninspected (uncited or island-suppressed) owner is empty or irrelevant. Also make the context explicit in the proposed renderer. The quoted-label path at source-literal-directive.ts:36-37 has no 'page'/'form' word in the criterion, so the PAGE vs FORM distinction is a plan assumption that must be specified.

findings.title: Iframe islands are not tracked at all
findings.evidence: Line 29 and line 51 skip iframe content. The parser's scriptingEnabled:true means that `<iframe srcdoc>` nested labels (which are active for no-embedding users and for some sanitizers) are never visited, and the fact that an island exists is not recorded. The proposal requires that foreign islands either be exactly parsed or cause absence to be disabled. The current function cannot tell the difference between 'no labels here' and 'an island was skipped here'.
findings.reproduction: Unexecuted reasoning trace. Parse `<iframe srcdoc="<form><label for=e>E-mail:</label><input id=e></form>"></iframe>` with a form descriptor. The parser visits the iframe and continues, because line 29's `continue` stops descent and no marker is set. labelsIn returns []. A proposal that gates only on the parser returning undefined would not fire.
findings.suggestion: Before descending in lines 29/51, set a parse-blocked flag when the skipped tag is one of the island tags (iframe and the five above). Pass that flag out of labelsIn, and have the renderer map it to unknown. An optional exact parse of the island subtree could then replace the flag.

limitations: Plan review only. No implementation, tests, typecheck, provider call or runtime execution was performed or observed. All traces are static reasoning over the supplied three source files, the fixture and the proposal.

Not supplied: exact-copy-directive.ts, static-markup-directive.ts (quotedSourceLabelLabels, staticMarkupLabelDirective), source-literal-directive tests, assessment-* checks other than the cited lines, and any tests for labelsIn. The behavior of the directive table and of the real PAGE/FORM routing is inferred from the cited lines only.

No unseen or live source corpus was supplied. The proposal's 'no omitted/truncated HTML sent' precondition cannot be verified from lib/assessment-label-citations.ts. sourcePacket (delivery-assessment.ts:68-83) sends all validated HTML/CSS without truncation. However, validateStaticFiles/delivery evidence and the assessmentCoverage omitted/truncated files are outside the supplied lines.
Only three fixture cases were available. They show the parse islands (template, script) and the cross-page split, but they are not a corpus of real or adversarial deliveries.

The product's strict status flow in delivery-assessment.ts:419-425 is unchanged by the proposal. The delivery of the new explanation is scoped to catalog_slots and skip-linked-business-checks only, per the proposal. The interaction with risks/publication policy (publishSourceAssessmentNotes) was not inspected.
Acceptance, payment, membership and approval behavior were not inspected and must not be treated as verified.
